result.topic_en: Using a Lagrange multiplier in a variational argument, the page shows that the force components are the gradient of a function λ under the incompressibility-type condition, and then derives Laplace-type equations for the displacements and expresses the forces as second time derivatives of the gradient of the potential V.
result.transcription:
(Substituirt man nämlich mit Hülfe der
ersten dieser beiden Gleichungen in der
andern eine der Variationen $\delta\eta_1', \delta\eta_2', \delta\eta_3'$
so müssen die Coefficienten der beiden {+übrigen+} [-andern-]
von einander unabhängigen Variationen
Null werden. Es giebt also ein $\lambda$, das mit
$\delta\frac{\partial\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_1}+\delta\frac{\partial\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_2}+\delta\frac{\partial\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_3}=0$ multiplicirt und dann
zum Integral addirt jeden der drei Coefficienten
zu von $\delta\eta_1', \delta\eta_2', \delta\eta_3'$ zu Null macht)
Aus den beiden Gleichungen folgt nämlich:
$\int\left(\begin{array}{l}X_1\delta\eta_1'+X_2\delta\eta_2'+X_3\delta\eta_3'\\+\lambda\left(\delta\frac{\partial\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_1}+\delta\frac{\partial\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_2}+\delta\frac{\partial\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_3}\right)\end{array}\right)d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=0$
$=\ldots+\int\left(\begin{array}{l}X_1\delta\eta_1'+X_2\delta\eta_2'+X_3\delta\eta_3'\\-\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial\eta_1}\delta\eta_1'+\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial\eta_2}\delta\eta_2'-\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial\eta_3}\delta\eta_3'\end{array}\right)d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=0$
also: $X_1-\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial\eta_1}=0$ ; $X_2-\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial\eta_2}=0$ ; $X_3-\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial\eta_3}=0$
d.h. $d\lambda=X_1d\eta_1+X_2d\eta_2+X_3d\eta_3$
also sind sämmtl. Bedingungen erfüllt.
(X) Für den von ponderabler Masse freien Raum
ist: $\frac{\partial^2V}{\partial\eta_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2V}{\partial\eta_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2V}{\partial\eta_3^2}=0$
da: $\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_1}=\eta_1'$ so ist auch: $\frac{\partial^2\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_3^2}=0$
$\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_2}=\eta_2'$ $\frac{\partial^2\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_3^2}=0$
$\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_3}=\eta_3'$ $\frac{\partial^2\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_1^3}+\frac{\partial^2\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_2^3}+\frac{\partial^2\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_3^3}=0$
Weil ferner in dem Falle wo nur Bewegungen {+der Art+} statt finden, die die Lichterscheinungen
hervorbringen: $X_1=X_2=X_3=0$ ist, so ist allgemein
$X_1=\frac{\partial^2\eta_1'}{\partial t^2}$ d.i. $=\frac{\partial^2\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_1}}{\partial t^2}$
$X_2=\frac{\partial^2\eta_2'}{\partial t^2}$ $=\frac{\partial^2\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_2}}{\partial t^2}$
$X_3=\frac{\partial^2\eta_3'}{\partial t^2}$ $=\frac{\partial^2\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_3}}{\partial t^2}$
also: $\int X_1d\eta_1+X_2d\eta_2+X_3d\eta_3=\frac{\partial^2V}{\partial t^2}$

methods.what: Force components are the gradient of the multiplier λ
Laplace equation for the potential V in matter-free space
Displacement components (gradient of V) are harmonic
Forces as second time derivatives of the gradient of V; their line integral equals ∂²V/∂t²
